You are part of a thorough, READ-ONLY audit of Nxeon, a LIVE VPS/game-server/web-hosting business. Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router + server actions + Prisma + Postgres). Read /opt/nxeon/CLAUDE.md first. Customer portal is app/dashboard/** (Shell: components/nx/Shell.tsx). Server actions live mostly in lib/actions*.ts; background work in worker/*.ts via `Job` rows.

STRICT RULES (live production): READ-ONLY. Do not edit/create/delete any file under /opt. Do not run npm/npx/tsc/prisma/build, any scripts/*, systemctl, pkill, or anything that mutates state. DB: SELECT-only via `sudo -u postgres psql -d nxeon -c "..."`, never write. Never print secrets, password hashes, tokens, API keys, or customer emails/PII (aggregate counts only). Do not touch the live site or submit forms.

YOUR SCOPE (customer portal sections, non-game): 
- app/dashboard/page.tsx (home) + lib/portal-home.ts
- app/dashboard/support (+[id]) — tickets: create, reply, attachments, close/reopen, notifications to staff and customer (lib/actions-support.ts, lib/ticket-*.ts, reply-core.ts)
- app/dashboard/team (+accept) and org/roles functionality: invite, accept, remove, role change (lib/actions-teams.ts, lib/team-guard.ts, lib/rbac.ts). NOTE the coordinator is separately checking whether roles grant real authorization on resource loaders; you check the invite/accept/remove flows work and whether invite emails are actually sent.
- app/dashboard/settings — profile, password change, 2FA (lib/actions-2fa.ts, totp*.ts), API keys/tokens (lib/actions-tokens.ts, lib/api-auth.ts — and does a public API actually exist that consumes the tokens? list app/api/v1 or similar routes and what they can do), sessions (can a user see/revoke sessions?), notification preferences (lib/actions-prefs.ts, prefs.ts — are prefs actually consulted by senders?), GDPR export/delete (actions-gdpr.ts), email verification, Discord link, Google login link.
- app/dashboard/activity, whats-new, feedback, calendar, directory, build, claude-code, projects, tools (+ each tools/* subpage), nxlabs (functionality only — does the mod catalog page load and link correctly; skip data quality), migrate (+consolidate, preview) (lib/actions-migrate.ts, worker/migrate*.ts, MIGRATE job).
For each, follow UI -> server action/API route -> worker and decide whether it truly works end-to-end. READ THE ACTUAL CODE.

Look specifically for: TODO/FIXME/"not implemented"/"coming soon"/stubs; server actions that return success without doing anything; errors caught and swallowed silently; buttons with no handler or hrefs to non-existent routes (verify each href target exists under /opt/nxeon/app/); features gated behind env flags (check /opt/nxeon/.env for flag NAMES only, never values: `grep -oE '^[A-Z_]+' /opt/nxeon/.env`); missing ownership checks (e.g. a ticket id from another user); 2FA bypasses (e.g. Google login or API token path skipping 2FA; password reset not requiring 2FA); API tokens that are shown in plaintext after creation/stored unhashed; session revocation not invalidating cookies; notification prefs that are never read; pages that are admin-ish or internal and shouldn't be customer-visible; pages in the nav/sidebar that are dead-ends.
Also: read components/nx/Shell.tsx (and its nav config) and list every nav link; check that each target exists and whether it's gated appropriately.
DB checks (SELECT only, aggregates): e.g. tickets by status and age of oldest unanswered, team invites by status, API token counts, 2FA adoption count, migrations by status. Check table names with \dt first.

DELIVERABLE (final message, no files): prioritized findings list. Each item: severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low), section, what's wrong/missing, evidence (file path:line or SQL result), why it matters to a paying customer, one-line fix direction. Then a short list of confirmed-working flows (one line each with evidence). Then gaps vs DigitalOcean/Hetzner/Vultr/Hostinger for account-level features (public API + docs, API token scopes, 2FA incl. recovery codes/WebAuthn, session management, audit log, team sub-users with real permissions, SSO, status page, notification channels like email/SMS/webhook/Slack) — absent / half-built / present with evidence. Be specific; don't pad.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).

- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.

- Wallet amounts are integer cents.
- Never fabricate: no invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, or ETAs. If a number can't be read from the database or a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why — this tree has had hash-derived star ratings and fake reviews removed once already.

## Domains & TLS

- **Single source of truth**: `/etc/nxeon/domains.env` (BASE_DOMAIN, ADMIN_HOST, STAGING_HOST, CERTBOT_EMAIL). The domain is a placeholder (`revsports.ca`) until the real one is bought. **Never hardcode the domain anywhere in app code** — the app uses `APP_URL` / `NXEON_ADMIN_HOST` from `.env`, and nginx vhosts are generated.
- **To migrate to a new domain**: edit `/etc/nxeon/domains.env`, point DNS (A records for apex, www, admin host, staging host) at the server, then run `scripts/configure-domains.sh`. HTTP→HTTPS 301. Real LE cert (auto-renews via certbot timer); self-signed fallback for bare-IP. A raw `http://51.79.162.96:8080` fallback listener also exists for staging (no TLS, no forwarded headers) — it's a debug path only, not how a real customer or any Server Action's origin check expects to be reached; testing against it directly produces false failures (CSP/origin-check errors) that don't reproduce on the real `STAGING_HOST`.

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.
- Test risky/provisioning changes on staging (`scripts/deploy-staging.sh`) before promoting to production.
- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

content.text:
Nxeon customer portal audit (non-game sections). This was read-only: I changed no files and ran only SELECT queries.

## Findings, most severe first

### High

**1. Google and Discord sign-in skip 2FA (Settings / login)**
- **What's wrong:** The authenticator-code check exists only in the password login, `lib/actions.ts:390`. The Google callback goes straight to `createSession` at `app/api/auth/google/callback/route.ts:183`. The Discord login does the same at `lib/discord-auth.ts:77` and `:118`.
- **Google also links silently by email:** it attaches itself to any existing account with that address (`:117-128`), including staff and admin accounts.
- **Evidence (DB):** 497 of 719 accounts signed up with Google. 56 accounts have Discord linked. 4 accounts have 2FA turned on and also a Google or Discord link, so their 2FA can be bypassed today.
- **Staff:** none of the 4 staff accounts has 2FA, and the `enforce_staff_2fa` setting is off.
- **Why it matters:** A customer who turned on 2FA is not protected when their Google account is compromised — the exact case 2FA exists for.
- **Fix:** When `totpEnabled` is true, the OAuth callbacks should create a pending-2FA state and ask for the code before calling `createSession`.

**2. API keys made in Settings don't work with the API (Settings, API)**
- **What's wrong:** The Settings page calls `lib/nx/account.ts:65-66`, which creates `nxk_live_…` keys in the `ApiKey` table.
- **What the API checks:** The only API route, `GET /api/v1/servers`, uses `lib/api-auth.ts`. That code accepts only `nxe_…` tokens and only looks them up in the `ApiToken` table (`:51`, `:57`). Nothing reads `ApiKey`.
- **The UI that made working tokens is dead:** `components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx` is not imported anywhere.
- **An invisible live token:** 1 `ApiToken` is still active and never used. The customer cannot see it or revoke it in the current UI.
- **Other problems:**
  - The `/developers` and `/docs` pages advertise scoped tokens and `nxe_live_…` keys.
  - The one endpoint returns `ip: s.ipAddress` (`route.ts:46`), which is the internal 10.20.x NAT address, and no SSH port.
- **Why it matters:** The public API is advertised but no customer can use it.
- **Fix:** Pick one table and one token format. Point Settings at `ApiToken` + `authorizeApiRequest`, and return the address from `connectAddress`.

**3. Account deletion leaves real services running and destroys billing records (Settings → Delete account)**
- **What's wrong:** `lib/actions-gdpr.ts:69` only checks for `Server` rows. Then `db.user.delete` (`:112`) removes, with no teardown job, these linked records:
  - hosting accounts, free Minecraft servers, email subscriptions
  - domains, volumes, NxCloud instances
  - invoices
- **Confirmation is weak:** only typing the email. There is no password or 2FA check, and no impersonation guard.
- **The UI copy is false:** it says "Every service has to be cancelled first" (`SettingsView.tsx:~745`).
- **Evidence (DB):** 35 accounts today have hosting, free Minecraft, email or a domain but no active server, so they can delete right now. 6 accounts have already deleted themselves.
- **Why it matters:**
  - Deleting orphans cPanel accounts, mailboxes and containers.
  - It wipes invoices that must be kept for tax.
  - Any leftover wallet balance is lost without warning.
- **Fix:** Block deletion while any service exists (or queue teardown jobs), keep invoices, require password + 2FA, and add `assertNotImpersonating`.

**4. Staff are barely told about new tickets (Support)**
- **What's wrong:** New tickets and customer replies only create an in-app notification for `role: "ADMIN"` (`lib/reply-core.ts:111`, `:206`). The 2 staff accounts with a `supportTickets` grant get nothing. No email is sent.
- **The admin's notification list is flooded:** 1,942 unread. Most are node alerts ("Node capacity CRITICAL" 532, memory pressure 521). 244 of the unread items are ticket notifications.
- **Evidence (DB):**
  - 1 OPEN ticket has had no reply for 243 hours (since 2026-09-14).
  - 1 ticket in customer-reply state since 09-19.
  - 5 tickets have never received a staff reply.
  - Both waiting tickets were mirrored to Discord.
- **Why it matters:** Paying customers wait days.
- **Fix:** Notify everyone who has support access (in-app and email), add an escalation for unanswered tickets, and move infrastructure alerts out of the same bell.

### Medium

**5. "Active sessions" list is always empty (Settings / Activity)**
- **What's wrong:** Nothing ever writes a `UserSession` row: the table has 0 rows and there is no create call anywhere.
- **Knock-on effects:** "Revoke" on a device (`lib/nx/account.ts:93`) does nothing. The Activity page's sign-in count always says "not recorded".
- **Logout:** it only deletes the cookie (`lib/auth.ts:50`), so a stolen session token stays valid for 30 days.
- **What does work:** "Sign out everywhere else", which bumps a per-account session counter.
- **Fix:** Record a session row in `createSession`, check it in `realUser`, and revoke it on logout.

**6. An admin impersonating a customer can end up fully logged in as them (Settings)**
- **What's wrong:** `signOutOtherSessions` (`lib/actions-account.ts:54`) and `changePassword` (`:32`) call `createSession(user.id)`, and during impersonation `user` is the customer.
- **Effect:** The admin's own session cookie is replaced by a normal 30-day customer session. The impersonation banner and the `assertNotImpersonating` protection on spending no longer apply, and the customer is signed out everywhere.
- **Fix:** Call `assertNotImpersonating()` in both.

**7. Customers silently miss staff reply emails (Support)**
- **What's wrong:** `TICKET_REPLY_DAILY_CAP = 5` (`lib/ticket-reply-email.ts:60`). Once a customer hits it, further reply emails are dropped for good. The catch-up sweep only looks back 30 minutes.
- **Evidence (DB):** 39 "Ticket reply emails paused" flags across 15 tickets (09-01 to 09-23). 5 `ticket_reply` emails FAILED.
- **Fix:** Send the held replies as a digest when the cap resets instead of dropping them.

**8. No security alert emails at all (Settings)**
- **What's wrong:** The `security_change` message type is declared in `lib/prefs.ts`, but nothing ever sends it.
- **Actions that send no email:** password change, 2FA disable, API key creation, new Google link, new sign-in.
- **Missing audit rows:** `changePassword` writes no audit entry, and neither does `createApiKey`.
- **Fix:** Send `security_change` emails from these actions.

**9. Unsupported claims on the dashboard home page**
- **Where:** `components/nx/DashboardView.tsx:59-61`.
- **"Support replies in ~4 min":** measured median first reply is 8.4 min, the mean is 98 min, and one ticket has waited 10 days.
- **"Restore a backup — any point in the last 7 days":** the free tier keeps only 2 daily backups (`lib/backup-tiers.ts`).
- **Rule broken:** CLAUDE.md forbids made-up ETAs.
- **Fix:** Compute the reply time from real data or remove it, and state the customer's actual backup retention.

**10. The Team page promises sharing that doesn't exist (Team)**
- **What the empty state says:** "Organisations let several people share one set of servers and services, each with … their own level of access" (`TeamView.tsx:127`).
- **What membership actually grants:** nothing beyond seeing the roster (`lib/actions-teams.ts:18-25`).
- **Invite bookkeeping bugs:**
  - `acceptInvite` never sets `OrgInvite.acceptedAt`, so accepted invites keep showing as pending and can still be "revoked".
  - The invite link expires after 72 hours, but the pending row says 7 days.
- **Missing:** no way to rename, transfer or delete an organisation.
- **Fix:** Correct the copy now; set `acceptedAt` when an invite is accepted.

**11. Display preferences save but change nothing (Settings)**
- **What's wrong:** Landing page, date format and rows per page are saved to `UserPreference` (`lib/nx/account.ts:27`), but nothing reads them. Only the theme is labelled as "not wired yet".
- **Fix:** Wire them up or hide them.

**12. GDPR data export is incomplete (Settings)**
- **Location:** `app/api/account/export/route.ts`.
- **Included today:** servers, wallet, invoices, domains, tickets, SSH keys, feedback, memberships.
- **Missing:** audit log, hosting, email, free Minecraft, chats and DMs, migrations, notifications, consent records.

**13. Migration is largely unproven in production (Migrate)**
- **Evidence (DB):** 57 runs, all from one customer account, and none since 2026-08-04.
  - 4 finished clean (DONE)
  - 33 finished with issues
  - 20 failed — 16 of those were refused by the source read-only guard
- **Consolidate:** it shows customers the internal env flag name `NXEON_CONSOLIDATE_REMAP` (which is unset) whenever two sources share a path (`lib/actions-migrate.ts`, `startConsolidationMigration`).
- **Partial runs:** the 5-per-10-minutes creation limit can leave a consolidation half-created.
- **Missing guards:** `createMigration` doesn't require the target server to be RUNNING or free of other in-flight jobs.
- **Fix:** Rehearse the full flow on staging, hide the flag name, and add the RUNNING / in-flight checks.

### Low
- **Mobile tab bar shows only "Dashboard":** the mobile list uses `"/deploy"`, `"/servers"`, `"/billing"`, but the nav entries are `/dashboard/...` (`components/nx/Shell.tsx:45`).
- **Feature flags no longer hide nav items:** the layout computes the filtered nav (`FEATURE_HREF` / `visibleNav` / `navWithBadges` in `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`) but never passes it to the new Shell. `/dashboard/claude-code` also doesn't check its flag.
- **No rate limits on tickets and feedback:** `createTicket`, `replyTicket` and `submitFeedback` are unthrottled. Each new ticket opens a Discord channel, and each reply can store up to 6 × 10 MB attachments in Postgres.
- **2FA weak spots:**
  - `disableTotp` accepts the account password alone.
  - No throttling on disable/confirm or on `changePassword`.
  - `regenerateBackupCodes` uses the check that doesn't block code reuse.
- **Ticket creation limits:** no attachments on a new ticket; customers can pick URGENT themselves.
- **Audit log IP never filled:** 0 of 2,105 rows in the last 30 days have an IP, so the Activity IP column is always blank.
- **Google login lands staff in the wrong place:** it sends EMPLOYEE accounts to `/dashboard` instead of `roleHome`. Its link-by-email rule also contradicts the Discord flow, which refuses to merge.
- **Dead-end copy:** the checkout message says to resend verification from "Settings → Email address", which has no resend button. The banner does work.
- **Short lists:** Support loads only 40 tickets with no paging; Activity is capped at 400 rows.
- **Dead code:** `components/customer/SecuritySettings.tsx` and `components/customer/TeamManager.tsx` are imported nowhere.

## Confirmed working (end to end)
- **Tickets:** create → ticket + message + admin bell + Discord mirror → `?ticket=` view.
  - Owner checks on reply, status change, thread and attachments (`actions-support.ts:95-97`, `:227`, `:334`; attachment route `:37`).
  - Attachments are validated and served safely (`nosniff`, CSP sandbox).
  - Staff reply → customer bell + email (156 sent).
- **Close / reopen:** customers can only set OPEN or CLOSED.
- **Team invites:** a real email is sent (2 `team_invite` sent) → the accept page requires the same address → membership created (2 accepted). The owner can't be demoted or removed, and a revoked invite is refused.
- **Password change and "Sign out everywhere else":** both invalidate other sessions. A password reset does not bypass 2FA at the next password login.
- **TOTP 2FA:**
  - Setup, confirm, 10 hashed backup codes, one-time backup-code use, codes can't be reused at login.
  - 8 accounts have it on.
- **Notification preferences are actually applied:** checked centrally in `sendMail` (`lib/mailer.ts:241`); unticking product news also removes the newsletter subscription.
- **Email verification resend:** rate-limited and reports the real result (191 sent, 15 failed).
- **Discord link / unlink:** refuses a Discord account already linked elsewhere.
- **GDPR export download:** own data only, secrets excluded.
- **Feedback:** submit → admin bell; status changes notify the reporter.
- **Projects:** create, and assign from the server page.
- **Nav and links:** all 21 sidebar links resolve, and every internal link in the scoped components points to an existing route.
- **Tools:** all 16 tool pages and 9 API routes exist, with a guard against internal-network lookups.
- **NxLabs:** catalog, game and mod pages link correctly and 404 on bad slugs.
- **Gated pages:**
  - Calendar returns 404 while `feature_calendar` is off.
  - Migrate preview is admin/sandbox only.
- **Migration safety:**
  - The worker won't fake a success if real migration is disabled (it is enabled).
  - No stored source passwords remain (0 rows).

## Account features vs DigitalOcean / Hetzner / Vultr / Hostinger
- **Public API + docs:** half-built. Docs pages exist, but there is one read-only endpoint and the keys the dashboard issues don't work with it. The others offer full create/read/update/delete APIs, OpenAPI specs and CLI/Terraform tooling.
- **API token scopes:** half-built. `ApiToken` supports read/write scopes and expiry but has no UI; the `ApiKey` scope field is decorative.
- **2FA:** TOTP + backup codes present. No WebAuthn/passkeys, bypassable through Google/Discord, and not enforced for staff.
- **Session management:** half-built. Global sign-out works; there is no per-device list or revoke, no new-login alerts, and logout doesn't revoke the session server-side.
- **Audit log:** present per user (Activity, 7/30/90 days). It only shows the viewer's own actions, has no IPs and no export, and there is no org-wide log.
- **Team sub-users with real permissions:** absent (roster only).
- **SSO (SAML/OIDC for customers):** absent. Only Google/Discord social login; Nxeon acts as a sign-in provider for the partner Kodely only.
- **Status page:** present (`/status`, incidents, per-component uptime, also inside Support).
- **Notification channels:** email + in-app only, plus a Discord bridge for support. No SMS, no customer webhooks (the `WebhookEndpoint` table is admin cold-email only), no Slack.
- **Self-service email change:** absent; the page says support must do it.
